Where the data come from and what to cite

Source: vignettes/articles/data-sources.Rmd
data-sources.Rmd

PaleoMapR contains no data. The setup downloads the open data sets below from their sources into the working folder; they keep their own licences and citation requests. If you publish maps made with PaleoMapR, please cite PaleoMapR (citation("PaleoMapR")) and the data behind the maps.

Elevation, coastlines and records

  • PaleoDEMs and the PALEOMAP plate model. 109 paleodigital elevation models, 0–540 Ma every 5 Myr, on a 0.2° grid (about 22 km); nothing finer exists in the source. Scotese, C. R. and Wright, N. (2018). PALEOMAP Paleodigital Elevation Models (PaleoDEMS) for the Phanerozoic. PALEOMAP Project. https://www.earthbyte.org/paleodem-resource-scotese-and-wright-2018/
  • PaleoCoastlines (version 7.2, Zenodo record 7828387): the PBDB-adjusted shorelines that the correction starts from. Kocsis, Á. T. and Scotese, C. R. (2021). Mapping paleocoastlines and continental flooding during the Phanerozoic. Earth-Science Reviews 213, 103463. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2020.103463
  • Fossil records: The Paleobiology Database, https://paleobiodb.org, downloaded through its data service (API 1.2). For each map age only collections whose age range covers that age ± 2.5 Myr are used; collections spanning more than 12 Myr are left out.
  • Rock units: Peters, S. E., Husson, J. M. and Czaplewski, J. (2018). Macrostrat: a platform for geological data integration and deep-time Earth crust research. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 19, 1393–1409. https://doi.org/10.1029/2018GC007467
  • Sea level: van der Meer, D. G., Scotese, C. R., Mills, B. J. W., Sluijs, A., van den Berg van Saparoea, A. P. and van de Weg, R. M. B. (2022). Long-term Phanerozoic global mean sea level: insights from strontium isotope variations and estimates of continental glaciation. Gondwana Research 111, 103–121. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2022.07.014
  • Present-day borders and coastlines: Natural Earth (public domain), https://www.naturalearthdata.com

Plate models and rotations

  • Rotations: GPlates / pyGPlates. Müller, R. D. et al. (2018). GPlates: building a virtual Earth through deep time. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 19, 2243–2261. https://doi.org/10.1029/2018GC007584
  • Other plate models, if you use them: Merdith, A. S. et al. (2021). Extending full-plate tectonic models into deep time: linking the Neoproterozoic and the Phanerozoic. Earth-Science Reviews 214, 103477. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.earscirev.2020.103477 · Torsvik, T. H. and Cocks, L. R. M. (2017). Earth History and Palaeogeography. Cambridge University Press. · The Golonka model as distributed by EarthByte (see models/golonka/readme.txt in the working folder).

Climate

PaleoMapR does not run a climate model. The climate layers are the output of the HadCM3L coupled atmosphere–ocean general circulation model (version HadCM3BL-M2.1aD; Valdes et al. 2017), run by the BRIDGE group of the University of Bristol for Valdes, Scotese & Lunt (2021). The series is scotese_02: 109 simulations from 541 Ma to 0 Ma on the PALEOMAP palaeogeographies of Scotese & Wright (2018), the same maps as the PaleoDEMs, with atmospheric CO2 after Foster, Royer & Lunt (2017). The run IDs go from texqe (541 Ma) to texpa1 (0 Ma). The Silurian runs:

Map age HadCM3L run Run age CO2 of the run
445 Ma teXPl 444.5 Ma 1708 ppm
440 Ma teXPk 441.2 Ma 1643 ppm
435 Ma teXPj 436.0 Ma 1576 ppm
430 Ma teXPi 430.4 Ma 1531 ppm
425 Ma teXPh 425.2 Ma 1490 ppm
420 Ma teXPg 421.1 Ma 1457 ppm
415 Ma teXPf 415.0 Ma 1579 ppm

For any map age the run closest in age is used, and the caption of every figure names the run, its age and CO2. The files (<run>a.pdcl<season>.nc atmosphere, <run>o.pfcl<season>.nc ocean) are the climatological means on the BRIDGE server, https://www.paleo.bristol.ac.uk/ummodel/data/<run>/climate/. The origin was checked against the BRIDGE run list of the series (https://www.paleo.bristol.ac.uk/ummodel/scripts/html_bridge/scotese_02.html) and the PhanDA HadCM3L model-prior record on Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/record/8237751), which lists scotese_02 as originally published in Valdes et al. (2021).

  • Climate: Valdes, P. J., Scotese, C. R. and Lunt, D. J. (2021). Deep ocean temperatures through time. Climate of the Past 17, 1483–1506. https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-17-1483-2021
  • Climate model: Valdes, P. J. et al. (2017). The BRIDGE HadCM3 family of climate models: HadCM3@Bristol v1.0. Geoscientific Model Development 10, 3715–3743. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-10-3715-2017
  • CO2 of the runs: Foster, G. L., Royer, D. L. and Lunt, D. J. (2017). Future climate forcing potentially without precedent in the last 420 million years. Nature Communications 8, 14845. https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms14845

The local correction. HadCM3L + local correction is PaleoMapR’s own statistical adjustment of the model fields to your corrected geography, learned from the same model run; it is not HadCM3L output. It captures continentality, moisture from new seaways, rain shadows and slower wind over new land, but not changes of the large-scale circulation. Say which climate option you used in your figure captions; the dashed outline on the maps marks where the climate is least reliable.
